Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Provide initial medical care to patients
Situation2: The ambulance driver is conducting a routine check of the first-aid kit to ensure all supplies are present and not expired.
Story: I was double-checking the first-aid kit in the back of the ambulance, making sure every bandage and vial was accounted for. My phone buzzed with a message from my daughter: “Don’t forget, we’re all counting on you to help organize the family dinner this weekend. The kids can’t wait to see you!” I smiled, picturing my grandchildren’s faces, but my hands kept moving, counting gauze pads and checking expiration dates. The holiday was always our time to reconnect, and I knew how much it meant to everyone, especially after the past year apart. But as I zipped up the kit, my radio crackled with a reminder about the importance of readiness—lives depended on it. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in: my family expecting my presence and warmth, my team and patients relying on my focus and precision. My heart tugged in two directions, and I stood there, torn, the ambulance humming quietly around me, my phone still glowing with my family’s hopes.
